subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (2, 0, 1) and (−1, 1, 5), and B is the matrix with rows (−1, 1, 0) and (0, 1, −2), then find (AB′)′.

mark_split.label: Find B′ and the product AB′

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find B′ and the product AB′
steps.margin_note: First mark. B is 2×3, so B′ is 3×2 — and A (2×3) times B′ (3×2) gives a 2×2. Check the sizes fit before multiplying.
steps.memory_tip: B is 2×3 so B′ is 3×2, and A (2×3) times B′ (3×2) gives a 2×2. Check the sizes fit first.

recall.must_convey: That B′ is the transpose of B, and AB′ is computed as a 2×2 matrix.
accept: transpose B then multiply A by B dash to get a two by two
B dash is three by two so A B dash is two by two
find the transpose first then the product
B transpose teeskoni A tho multiply cheyyali

steps.why: A is 2×3 and B is 2×3, so AB is not defined — transposing B is what makes the multiplication possible at all.

steps.label: Transpose the result
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Transpose the 2×2 just found — rows become columns.
steps.memory_tip: Transpose the 2×2 just found — rows become columns.

recall.must_convey: That the 2×2 product is transposed, giving rows (−2, 2) and (−2, −9).
accept: transpose the product so rows become columns
the answer has rows minus two two and minus two minus nine
take the transpose of what was just found
product ni transpose cheste answer vasthundi
the final answer is the transposed product

steps.why: The outer dash applies to the whole product, so it is done last. (AB′)′ also equals BA′ by the reversal law — a useful check if time allows.
common_mistakes: Reversing the rows instead of exchanging rows with columns.
